rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=bilateral, bilateral_on_top=False, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=30, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=1, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-25 param_efficient breast -- CONJUGATE-GRADIENT DATA-CONSISTENCY (highest-upside untested lever). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: champion = LPD-combine W=4 + FILTERED-DC (single fbp(Rx-g)) K=30, 5-seed mean 0.4590+-0.0294 @ 183p (best 0.5047). Filtered-DC uses ONE filtered gradient per step; a proper CG solve of the normal equations is a MUCH stronger DC solver -- CG-DC is the mechanism that got fastdiff-pixel-DC-on to 0.52 and wavelet-DC-on to 0.28. UNTESTED in this unroll. (2) FAILURE MODE: a single filtered gradient only partially enforces Rx=g each step; 30 of them approximate consistency but a per-step CG solve nails it far better. (3) ONE KNOB (architectural): dc_mode 'filtered'->'cg' -- I added CGDataConsistency: n_cg=5 matrix-free CG iterations solving (R^T R + lam I)d = R^T(g - Rx) for the DC update d (lam = softplus(learnable), damps the ill-conditioned 128-view normal operator), fed to the SAME LPD-combine block. +1 param (lam) -> 184 total. NOT byte-for-byte the champion (CG is a different, stronger DC operator) -- it is a genuine architectural swap of the DC solver. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a per-step CG least-squares DC solve enforces Rx=g much more completely than one filtered gradient, so the LPD-combine routes a cleaner, more consistent correction -> hr climbs past 0.5047 toward the 0.52-0.63 regime (fastdiff CG-DC reached 0.52). Risk: CG on the ill-conditioned 128-view operator can amplify streaks if underdamped -> lam is learnable to control this. (5) BUDGET: 5 CG iters = 5 fwd+back-proj PAIRS per unroll step x K=30 -> ~10x the projector calls of filtered-DC; may only fit a few epochs in 1080s -- if hr promising but undertrained, iter-26 reduces cg_n or K. train_n=200, --time=00:30:00, 200-val, 20-min budget. (6) SERIAL; iter-26: tune cg_n/lam if it helps, then multi-scale-bilateral POST-filter., dc_mode=cg, per_step_alpha=True, lpd_on=True, lpd_width=4, lpd_kernel=3, anisotropic_on_top=False, cg_n=5, cg_lam_init=0.01

Wu-init (iter-22) was a null for INITIALIZATION, but Wu's distinctive value is FREQUENCY-BAND SELECTIVITY, which the uniform ramp lacks. (2) FAILURE MODE: uniform ramp-filtered DC cannot down-weight streak-frequency components while preserving detail-frequency. (3) ONE KNOB (architectural): dc_mode 'filtered'->'band' -- I added a BandWeightedDC module: it reweights the residual spectrum by Sum_i s_i*tri_i(f) (tri_i = triangular partition-of-unity band windows, Sum tri_i=1) BEFORE the projector's fbp. s_i init 1.0 => reweight == identity => dc == fbp(resid) == the 0.5047 champion BYTE-FOR-BYTE at init (no regression). +6 band-scale params -> 189 total. All else byte-for-byte iter-15 (LPD W=4, K=30, seed42). OR the s_i train back toward 1.0 (uniform ramp already captures the useful spectrum) -> clean null. (5) BUDGET: band reweight = 1 FFT/iFFT per step (cheap); iter-15 finished 16ep in 1020s -> expect ~14-16ep; train_n=200, max_train_s=1080, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min comparable. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a learned dual that preconditions the residual in measurement space (the true primal-dual structure) lets the unroll route sparse-view inconsistency where it lives -> hr climbs past 0.5047 toward VN 0.63 / LPD 0.68, at ~296 params. (5) BUDGET: +1 tiny sinogram conv/step (sinogram is A*D ~ 128*736, similar cost to the image conv); iter-15 finished 16ep in 1020s -> expect ~14-16ep in the 1080s wall; train_n=200, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min comparable. rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=bilateral, bilateral_on_top=False, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=30, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=1, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-15 param_efficient breast -- LPD-STYLE LEARNED DUAL/COMBINATION block (last distinct arch lever, solver edit, 20-min budget). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: filtered-DC K=30 = 20-min CHAMPION 0.4345 @ 13p. Added PROX capacity does NOT help it: iter-13 (isotropic FoE +300p) hr 0.0, iter-14 (directional aniso +3p) hr 0.0 -- both FIGHT the filtered gradient because fbp(Rx-g) already does the reconstruction, leaving nothing for a prox to add. So the remaining lever is not a better PROX but a better way to COMBINE the DC correction across steps -- LPD's mechanism (0.68 on breast). (2) FAILURE MODE: the fixed x<-x-alpha*fbp(resid) update applies the SAME correction rule every step; it cannot learn to weight/route the correction using image context or cross-step memory. (3) ONE KNOB (architectural): lpd_on=True -- I added a minimal LPDCombine block: a weight-tied 2-layer 3x3 conv g(x, fbp_dc, mem)->update (3->W=4->1, 149 params) with a 1-ch primal MEMORY carried across the 30 steps; final layer ZERO-INIT => update==0 at init => x stays at the FBP init (safe seed, already clears baseline). per_step_alpha=True (the K alphas now scale the LEARNED update per step -- a real role, not the collapsed scalars of iter-7). Total ~= 149 (conv) + 30 (per-step alpha) + 12 (bilateral, UNUSED in LPD path) ~= 190 trainable. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a tiny learned operator that COMBINES the filtered-DC correction with image context + cross-step memory (LPD's mechanism) breaks past 0.4345 toward the LPD/VN regime, because it learns HOW to apply consistency (route/attenuate per-pixel + accumulate) rather than a fixed step -- the capacity that helps DC, unlike a prox smoother. (5) BUDGET: K=30 filtered + 1 tiny conv/step + 1 fbp/step, train_n=200, max_train_s=1080, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min comparable. (6) SERIAL; iter-16: if LPD beats 0.4345, grow W / tune; if not, 0.4345 @ 13p is the honest comparable champion -> CONSOLIDATE the final report (Pareto + filtered-vs-adjoint-DC + capacity-doesnt-help-filtered-DC findings)., dc_mode=filtered, per_step_alpha=True, lpd_on=True, lpd_width=4, lpd_kernel=3, anisotropic_on_top=False

READ: a learned FoE ISOTROPIC smoother FIGHTS filtered-DC -- fbp(Rx-g) already produces a complete ramp-filtered reconstruction each step, so an added smoothing prior just OVER-SMOOTHS the recon the DC just made (the FoE solves the streak-smearing problem filtered-DC ALREADY solved -> pure drag). So on filtered-DC, isotropic prox capacity is a LIABILITY. (2) FAILURE MODE (iter-13): isotropic prox over-smooths the filtered-DC reconstruction. (4) HYPOTHESIS: unlike the isotropic FoE, the oriented reg smooths ALONG residual streak directions while PRESERVING across them, so it removes the specific directional streaks filtered-DC leaves WITHOUT the isotropic over-smoothing that killed iter-13 -> hr climbs past 0.4345. This is the sparse-view-NATIVE prox form (streaks are directional). (5) BUDGET: K=30 filtered + lean bilat + aniso (analytic oriented kernels, cheap), train_n=200, max_train_s=1080, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min comparable. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: steps 8 vs 16 identical (rmse0.01130 vs 0.01131) -> NFE not the limiter, prior is the ceiling. Best t=0.5 eta=0.0 steps=8. All hr=0; DC-off floor ~0.0113. (2) Failure mode: FBP-warm-start recons plateau; unknown = how much the FBP init contributes vs the prior alone. (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_init fbp->noise (start from pure N(0,I) at t=1, no FBP warm-start), eta=0.0 steps=8. (4) HYPOTHESIS: with NO FBP anchor and eta=0 (no DPS), the recon is UNCONDITIONAL prior sampling -> rmse MUCH worse (the prior draws a plausible breast, not THIS one). This bounds the pure-generative extreme and shows the FBP warm-start is what keeps DC-off recon near-usable. Confirms the prior alone cannot solve the inverse problem. (5) BUDGET: noise-init 8-step still <10min. (6) Loop continues.

rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=bilateral, bilateral_on_top=False, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=10, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-9 param_efficient breast -- ARCHITECTURAL CHANGE: FILTERED-GRADIENT DC (I edited the solver, per coordinator: everything is changeable). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: 8 iters prove the ADJOINT GD-unroll caps at image-domain ~0.26 on sparse-view; the diagnosis (iter-6) is that R^T(Rx-g) back-projects a STREAKY residual -> re-injects coherent streaks -> deeper adjoint DC LOWERED hr. That is an ARCHITECTURAL ceiling, not a config one. (2) FAILURE MODE: the raw adjoint DC operator smears sparse-view streaks. (3) ONE KNOB (architectural): dc_mode 'adjoint'->'filtered' -- I added a config-gated branch in ParamEfficientUnrolled._grad so the DC direction is fbp(Rx-g) (ramp/Hann-filtered residual back-projection = a PROPER reconstruction correction, the SART/FBP-gradient trick) instead of R^T(Rx-g)/dc_norm. ZERO extra params; touches only my solver, not the projector/metrics. Applied on the LEAN prox (bilateral 3-scale, 13 params) at K=10 depth -- because a filtered gradient should make DEPTH help (the exact lever the adjoint poisoned in iter-6). (4) HYPOTHESIS: because the ramp-filtered residual correction does NOT smear streaks, 10 filtered-DC steps drive Rx->g while actually REMOVING the coherent streaks (each step reconstructs the residual properly) -> hr breaks past 0.264 toward the VN/LPD regime, at ~13-22 params. This is the minimal architectural fix my own evidence points to. (5) BUDGET: filtered DC = 1 extra fbp per step vs adjoint's back_project (similar cost); K=10 bilateral, train_n=200, 1080s backstop + 200-val -> <20min. (6) SERIAL; iter-10 self-dispatches (next: if filtered-DC helps, sweep K / add the FoE or proj-filter on top; if not, LPD dual)., dc_mode=filtered, per_step_alpha=False

Locks the best config found: init_t0.01, n_cg20, relax1.0, steps8, eta1.0 (iter-15, hr=0.5164, rmse0.002522, psnr42.63, ssim0.978 - HALF the FBP baseline rmse0.00521). SEARCH SUMMARY: the breast-native prior + few-step flow with a deep-but-not-over-converged CG data-consistency step (DC-ON constrained variant) CLEARS the strong 128-view breast FBP baseline by a wide margin. This confirms the FAIR TEST: prior-mismatch (Mayo out_scale0.05 vs breast0.5) WAS the cause of the old hr=0; a matched breast-native prior lifts pixel-DC-on to hr~0.52. Confirmation run reproduces the champion (deterministic seed=42).

rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=foe, bilateral_on_top=True, proj_filter_on=True, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-8 param_efficient breast -- PROJECTION-DOMAIN FILTER ON (sparse-view-native lever). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: 7 iters prove the config-only GD-unroll caps at image-domain ~0.26. iter-7 per_step_alpha gave IDENTICAL 0.1897 to iter-2 -- the 5 per-step alphas COLLAPSED to one shared value; the loss landscape has no incentive to differentiate them, so config-only per-step-alpha CANNOT express a genuine VN. Combined with iter-6 (deeper DC WORSE = streak re-injection), verdict: the image-domain DC gradient R^T(Rx-g) is corrupting on 128-view sparse and no image-side knob escapes ~0.26. (2) FAILURE MODE: image-domain-only ceiling; the DC gradient re-injects streaks; no config knob learns to combine it. (3) ONE KNOB: proj_filter_on False->True (Manduca sinogram bilateral, +5 params: 3 sigma + log_N0 + 1 zero-init gain). It denoises the LOG-SINOGRAM on the Anscombe sqrt-count (noise-adaptive) BEFORE the FBP init, then recomputes x0 from the FILTERED sino, so it removes streak-CAUSING projection inconsistencies at the SOURCE rather than fighting them in image space. On dense Mayo this was null (FBP already averages proj noise); on 128-view SPARSE it is the native lever. All else byte-for-byte iter-2 (FoE+bilateral K5). (4) HYPOTHESIS: cleaning the sinogram before back-projection reduces the coherent streaks the FBP init injects, so the FoE+DC unroll starts from a cleaner image and hr exceeds 0.264, because sparse-view streaks are a PROJECTION-domain defect and this is the one lever VN/LPD lack. Zero-init gain => at init pipeline==iter-2 byte-for-byte (worst case == 0.190, no regression). (5) BUDGET: +1 sinogram bilateral per forward (cheap vs the K=5 image unroll); train_n=200, 1080s backstop + 200-val -> <20min. (6) SERIAL; iter-9 self-dispatches (next: if proj-filter helps, TUNE its sigma_r/gain or make it multi-scale; if not, directional streak reg +3p)., proj_n_bf=1, proj_multiscale=False, proj_kernel=5, proj_sigma_x=0.83, proj_sigma_y=0.83, proj_sigma_r=1.5, proj_gain_init=0.0, proj_N0=100000.0, per_step_alpha=False

rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=foe, bilateral_on_top=True, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-7 param_efficient breast -- LEARNED PER-STEP DC WEIGHT (step toward VN). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: 6 iters map the plain tied-GD unroll. KEY new finding iter-6: deep DC (K20) on the lean prox gave hr 0.0 -- DEEPER DC made it WORSE (0.066->0.0), not better. So the problem is NOT under-consistency: on 128-view sparse data the DC gradient R^T(Rx-g) itself is CORRUPTING -- with only 128 views R^T R is a STREAKY operator, so back-projecting the residual RE-INJECTS coherent streaks; iterating it 20x AMPLIFIES exactly what we want removed. This is why LPD (primal-dual) + VN (learned per-step gradient weighting) win and a plain repeated R^T(Rx-g) GD unroll caps ~image-domain. Best point stays iter-1 0.264 (FoE capacity as image cleanup). (2) FAILURE MODE: raw tied DC gradient amplifies streaks over steps; a SINGLE shared scalar alpha can't attenuate the harmful later steps. (3) ONE KNOB: per_step_alpha False->True on the FoE+bilateral K5 arch (iter-2 base, the fully-trained 0.190 config). +4 params (5 per-step alphas vs 1) -> ~1937 total. This is the MINIMAL move from plain-GD toward VN: each step learns its OWN DC weight, so the net can DOWN-WEIGHT the streak-amplifying later steps. (4) HYPOTHESIS: learned per-step alphas let the unroll learn to apply DC strongly early (coarse consistency) then softly late (avoid streak re-injection), rescuing the fully-trained FoE from the over-regularize/corrupt regime -> hr exceeds 0.264, because per-step DC weighting is VN's core trick and it directly targets the iter-6 corruption finding. (5) BUDGET: K=5 FoE+bilateral, train_n=200, 1080s backstop + 200-val -> <20min (same cost as iter-2). (6) SERIAL; iter-8 self-dispatches (next: if per-step helps, sweep K deeper WITH per-step alphas; if not, projection-domain filter +5p)., per_step_alpha=True

rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=bilateral, bilateral_on_top=False, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=20, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-6 param_efficient breast -- DC DEPTH on the lean prox. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-5 (pivot: reg foe->bilateral, 13 params, K5) hr 0.0664 -- cleared baseline (PSNR 36.92>36.32), ran ALL 16 epochs stably, alpha auto-tuned to 0.022. But 0.066 < iter-1's 0.264 AND < the bilateral-alone-no-DC ceiling 0.26-0.28. Read: at K=5 five weak DC steps + a light gate do too LITTLE work; the prox can't over-smooth (good) but the shallow DC removes few streaks. iter-4's K=12 collapse was the FoE over-regularizing, NOT the depth -- the light bilateral gate CAN'T over-smooth, so deep DC should now compound productively. (2) FAILURE MODE: under-consistency -- the DC-dominant compact is too SHALLOW (K=5) to null the sparse-view residual. (3) ONE KNOB: n_iter 5 -> 20 (deep weight-TIED DC unroll on the 13-param bilateral prox). WEIGHT-TIED => still 13 params. All else byte-for-byte iter-5. (4) HYPOTHESIS: 20 tied DC steps with a non-over-smoothing bilateral gate drive Rx->g far enough to remove coherent streaks -> hr rises WELL past 0.264 (and past iter-5's 0.066), because on the LEAN prox depth is the free lever that FoE poisoned in iter-4. This is VN's mechanism (learned reg + genuine DC + weight-share) in 13 params. (5) BUDGET: K=20 bilateral is ~4x the round-trips of iter-5's K5 but bilateral is cheap per step; iter-5 finished 16ep in 465s so K20 ~fits several epochs under the 1080s backstop; 200-val pass fits; <20min guaranteed by backstop. (6) SERIAL; iter-7 self-dispatches (next: sweep alpha_init on the STABLE deep-DC lean prox, then proj-domain +5p).

rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=bilateral, bilateral_on_top=False, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-5 param_efficient breast -- ARCHITECTURE PIVOT (drop Mayo FoE). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: 4 negatives converge -- iter1(K5,a.09,3ep) 0.264 BEST; iter2(11ep) 0.190; iter3(a0.5) 0.0 diverge; iter4(K12) 0.0 over-regularize. EVERY direction that engages the FoE reg MORE lowers hr; best result had FoE LEAST trained. Verdict: the Mayo FoE is a NOISE prior added INSIDE the GD step (x=x-alpha*(dc+reg)) so a trained FoE smoother directly CORRUPTS the DC direction on coherent streaks. (2) FAILURE MODE: reg-DC conflict -- the FoE fights consistency; it is the ceiling, not the help. (3) ONE KNOB: reg_type foe -> bilateral (standalone 3-scale edge-preserving gate, 12 reg params, bilateral_on_top=False). K=5, alpha=0.1, train_n=200 else byte-for-byte iter-2. The range kernel (sigma_r=0.02) STRUCTURALLY vetoes over-smoothing (coordinator: DD-bf-N2I 0.21 vs plain-N2I 0.00) so it CAN'T corrupt DC the way FoE did. (4) HYPOTHESIS: replacing the FoE noise prior with a light bilateral gate lets the genuine DC unroll DOMINATE -- streaks get removed by re-imposing Rx=g while the gate only preserves edges, so hr rises past 0.264 at just 12 reg params (13 total). Note: bilateral ALONE (no DC) capped 0.28 on breast; the bet is that WITH the K=5 DC unroll it does better because DC does the streak removal. (5) BUDGET: K=5 bilateral is CHEAPER than FoE per step -> more epochs fit 1080s wall; 200-val pass fits; <20min. (6) SERIAL; iter-6 self-dispatches (next: DC depth K on THIS lean prox, then projection-domain filter +5p).

(5) BUDGET: train_n=200 K=5 bs4 + 200-val, 1080s backstop -> <20min. (6) SERIAL; iter-4 self-dispatches (next: projection-domain filter ON -- sparse-view-native).

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=1, train_n=400, n_iter=60, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.003, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=iter-19 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: pretrain_epochs 2->1 (SHORTER warm-start), on CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, lr=3e-3, n_iter=60; iter-15 hr=0.2056). warm-start DEPTH now shows a NON-MONOTONE sweet spot: 0 epochs (warm_start=False, iter-17) -> hr=0.0025 CRASH (no seed); 2 epochs (iter-15) -> 0.2056 PEAK; 5 epochs (iter-18) -> 0.0403 CRASH. The 5-epoch collapse = the AMORTISED warm-start ITSELF over-smooths (the N2I-over-smoothing bias operates in the warm-start pre-pass too, using the WIDE default sigmas), seeding a blurred init the tight per-scene img_sr cannot recover. So the warm-start must be SHORT: enough to seed, not enough to over-smooth. HYPOTHESIS: 1 epoch is even less over-smoothed than 2 while still providing the essential non-crash seed -> hr >= 0.2056 (possibly higher if 2 epochs already began mild over-smoothing). If hr < 0.2056, 2 epochs is the sweet spot (1 under-seeds). This MAPS the warm-start sweet spot precisely for the paper. WALL: pretrain 2->1 SAVES warm steps, ~950-1000s, val_n~196-200. ONE knob: pretrain_epochs 2->1.

(1) PRIOR: iter-7 hr=0.0, aggressive lr=3e-3 (n_iter=50) gave rmse=0.00657 (WORST of the run), ssim=0.931 -- the big step destabilized/over-smoothed. Best config remains iter-6: lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, rmse=0.00628. (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I regresses to the over-smoothed FBP mean; large lr worsens it. (3) ONE KNOB: relative to the BEST reference config (iter-6: warm_start=True, lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, pretrain_epochs=3), change ONLY pretrain_epochs 3 -> 10 (revert lr to iter-6's 3e-4). A stronger amortised warm-start = a better generic init for the 50-step per-image fits. (4) HYPOTHESIS: 10 warm-start epochs on the 400-scene train split give the denoisers a stronger, more detail-aware initialization, so the short 50-step per-image fit starts from a sharper point and lands at lower rmse. If hr rises, the warm-start init quality was the lever. Per the documented ceiling, more likely the amortised N2I warm-start ALSO converges to an over-smoothed mean (same GT-free FBP target), so a stronger warm-start just entrenches the blur (hr=0). (5) BUDGET: pretrain ep=10 (~430s) + 200*50-step fast fits (~400s) + figure ~= 15 min < 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-9 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: unet_c=8 (smaller), n_iter=100 mid, grad_clip off, seed variance check, pretrain_steps cap.

With warm_start=False each scene fits from the CONFIG init (img_sr=0.0002 exactly) -> if hr >= 0.2056 the warm-start is UNNECESSARY (pure per-image N2I is self-sufficient AND drops the train-set dependency, a cleaner self-supervised story: train_n=0); if hr DROPS, the warm-start init genuinely helps the 60-step fit converge and should be kept. (1) PRIOR: iter-6 hr=0.0, early-stop n_iter=50 (lr=3e-4) gave rmse=0.00628 (marginally best, still >> baseline 0.00521), ssim=0.942, 200/200. Stopping early froze a still-blurry recon -- the warm-started init is already over-smoothed. Iters 1-6 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity, warm-start, lr-down, early-stop) all hr=0. NOTE: the SIBLING solver dual_domain_bilateral_n2i (a DIFFERENT solver with a trainable bilateral post-filter) reached hr~0.20; that bilateral edge-preserving stage is exactly the structural element THIS plain-UNet N2I solver lacks -- documented as the likely reason for our ceiling, but out of scope to add (protocol fixes SOLVER=dual_domain_n2i). (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I regresses to the over-smoothed FBP-consistent mean; no edge-preserving prior to hold detail. (3) ONE KNOB: lr 3e-4 -> 3e-3 (keep n_iter=50, warm_start=True, c=16 -- identical to iter-6 except lr, an order-of-magnitude aggressive step). (4) HYPOTHESIS: a large step size with only 50 inner iters may jump the per-image fit into a sharper, higher-frequency basin the small-lr fits never reached, lowering rmse; if hr rises, the plateau was an optimization-basin artifact. Per the ceiling, more likely lr=3e-3 either destabilizes (grad_clip=1.0 catches it) or converges to the same over-smoothed solution (hr=0). (5) BUDGET: 50 inner steps/scene, fast; loop << 1400s wall; total ~13 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-8 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: pretrain_epochs up (10), unet_c=8, n_iter mid (100), grad_clip off, seed change (variance check).

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=50, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-6 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-5 hr=0.0, lr 1e-3->3e-4 gave rmse=0.00633 (best yet, but still >> baseline 0.00521), ssim=0.941, 197/200. Gentler steps nudged rmse down ~1% -- not near baseline. Iters 1-5 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity, warm-start, lr) all pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: N2I converges toward the over-smoothed FBP-consistent mean; the self-supervision target caps recon RMSE above the sparse-FBP baseline. A known N2I pathology on dense phantoms is that MORE inner steps over-smooth MORE (the denoiser regresses to the low-frequency mean). (3) ONE KNOB: n_iter 200 -> 50 (early-stop; keep lr=3e-4, c=16, warm_start=True -- identical to iter-5 except inner-step count). (4) HYPOTHESIS: stopping the per-image fit early (50 steps) may HALT before the denoiser collapses to the over-smoothed mean, preserving more high-frequency detail from the warm-started init and LOWERING rmse toward baseline. If hr rises, over-smoothing is a late-optimization effect and early-stop is the lever. HYPOTHESIS: the N2I self-sup target is the noisy 64-view half-FBP, so each Adam step pulls the BF PARTLY toward that noise floor; at lr=5e-3 the 30-step fit may OVERSHOOT the sweet spot (denoised but sharp) toward the noisy target. A gentler lr=2e-3 lets the fit settle MORE PRECISELY at the edge-preserving optimum before drifting toward noise -> hr could edge above 0.126. If FLAT/DROP, the 30-step fit is already well-damped and lr is neutral -> the ~0.126 plateau is the genuine edge-preserving N2I ceiling on dense breast. BUDGET: same step count, ~700-950s, val_n=200 expected. ONE knob: lr 0.005->0.002.

Iters 1-4 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity, warm-start on/off) ALL pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: structural over-smoothing set by the 128-view FBP self-supervision target, independent of budget/capacity/init. (3) ONE KNOB: lr 1e-3 -> 3e-4 (back to warm_start=True, c=16, n_iter=200 -- identical to iter-2 except lr). (4) HYPOTHESIS: a gentler per-image step size may let the N2I fit settle into a sharper local optimum instead of over-shooting into an over-smoothed mean; if hr rises, the over-smoothing was partly an optimization/step-size artifact. Per the documented ceiling, more likely lr just changes convergence speed and the SAME over-smoothed solution is reached (hr=0), since the target itself is the limiter. (5) BUDGET: identical compute profile to iter-2 (warm-start ep=3 + 200*7.0s + figure ~= 26 min < 30-min wall). (6) Loop continues; iter-6 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: lr up (3e-3), n_iter early-stop (50), pretrain_epochs up (10), unet_c=8, grad_clip variation.

R2-Gaussian is REGIME-BOUNDED on dense 128-view breast: the coarse anisotropic-Gaussian basis (1024 splats, 0.006M params) plateaus at SSIM ~0.928 / PSNR ~28.7 dB, ~7.3 dB BELOW the 128-view FBP baseline (PSNR 35.97), so the RMSE/PSNR-gated headroom stays 0 (reproduces findings.md 2026-06-03). All 7 lever families mapped+exhausted (steps FLAT, capacity +0.010, warm-start +0.039, SSIM-loss +0.073, SSIM-weight saturated, basis-scale FLAT, TV-reg FLAT); NONE moves hr off 0 -- the strongest (warm-start + SSIM-loss) got closest but stayed 7.3 dB short. The R2-G paper's regime is SPARSE-view CBCT (<=50 views) where FBP is weak; dense 128-view 2D CT is the wrong inductive bias. DECISION: empty-patch re-run of the iter-6 run-best config (warm-start + SSIM-loss@0.30, 1024G/130it) to confirm SSIM ~0.928 / hr=0 reproduces. BUDGET: ~660-1000s node-dependent, under the 1080 in-solver wall and 1800 SLURM wall, figure excluded. val_n=15 HELD CONSTANT. Spatial sigma REVERTED to default 1.5 (iter-9 widen 1.5->2.5 gave hr=0.1140 < champ 0.1261 -> widening blurs fibroglandular detail; spatial axis does NOT want to widen). CHAMPION = iter-7 hr=0.1261 SSIM0.9606 (val_n=200). HYPOTHESIS: iter-9 showed breast fine structure is DAMAGED by a wider spatial support -> the recon wants the SHARPEST possible spatial averaging. A 5x5 kernel (vs 7x7) confines the BF to immediate neighbours, denoising flat noise while preserving the finest fibroglandular edges better than 7x7 -> hr could edge above 0.1261. If FLAT/DROP, 7x7 is already fine (the tight range sigma, not the window, sets edge-preservation) and kernel is neutral. SECONDARY BENEFIT: 5x5 unfold is FASTER than 7x7 -> keeps the per-image loop under outer_wall_s=900 so val_n stays a clean 200 (iters 8/9 trimmed to 193 under heavier configs, confounding hr). BUDGET: smaller kernel -> ~700-900s, no wall trim expected. ONE knob: img_kernel 7->5.

BUDGET: spatial-sigma cost is independent of VALUE (same 7x7 kernel unfold); ~700-1000s like iter-7. ONE knob: img_sx/img_sy 1.5->2.5.

(4) HYPOTHESIS: removing the amortised warm-start tests whether the pre-pass was pulling every scan toward an over-smoothed mean. If pure per-image N2I clears hr>0, warm-start was the culprit.
